entries.title: Schumer Super PAC Drops $2 Million in Senate Democrats’ First Texas Spend
entries.summary: The amount pales compared to the $130 million Senate Majority Leader John Thune’s super PAC has spent so far in the state.
entries.content:
A new arm of Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s political committee on Thursday disclosed $2.1 million in spending on an ad against Texas Republican Ken Paxton. It’s the first major spending by Democratic leadership in the state’s Senate race — but a drop in the bucket compared to Republicans’ investments over the past month.

The Senate Majority PAC’s affiliate committee, Texas Forever, spent the money on a digital ad that dropped Tuesday. The spot addresses Paxton’s handling of a controversial plea deal in a high-profile child sex abuse case, in which the state attorney general reduced former Waco defense attorney Adam Hoffman’s charges in exchange for his guilty pleas of sexually abusing his son’s friend.

“Ken Paxton is dangerously corrupt for Texas,” the ad says, saying Paxton awarded Hoffman an “Epstein-style deal to let a pedophile walk free.”

The new ad buy pales in comparison to Republicans’ spending in the state — particularly by Senate Majority Leader John Thune, whose Senate Leadership Fund super PAC has disclosed $130 million in Texas spending since September, a number that will likely balloon as Nov. 3 draws closer.

Spending habits in the state reflect intertwining anxieties within both parties about Democrats’ chances of winning a Senate seat for the first time since 1988.

Democrats historically haven’t spent significant amounts of money in Texas’ expensive media market, and the party is currently facing a major cash crunch. But the National Republican Senatorial Committee and Thune’s super PAC have also had to increasingly direct more resources to what should be a reliably red seat, especially as state Rep. James Talarico maintains a tight polling lead.

President Donald Trump kicked off his ambitious midterm campaign blitz in Durant, Oklahoma, and Denton, Texas, on Thursday in hopes of amplifying Republicans’ accomplishments in already red states.

But even the president’s preferred candidate hasn’t garnered much enthusiasm: Despite party leaders’ pleas for him to get more financially involved in the tight race, Trump has only disclosed spending about $20 million for Paxton, whom he endorsed over Sen. John Cornyn this spring.

“He can be a pain in the ass sometimes, I’ll be honest,” Trump said while praising Paxton during his Texas speech Thursday, asking if the state attorney general was even in the room. “Oh, there he is. I didn’t even know if he’s here — I don’t care.”
entries.author: Marissa Martinez

entries.title: MLB Drops the Idea for a Game at Grand Teton National Park
entries.summary: Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred said local opposition prompted the decision.
entries.content:
MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred on Thursday scrapped an idea to field a baseball game in Grand Teton National Park after locals rejected the league’s interest as “hostile” to public lands.

In a letter to Wyoming officials Thursday, Manfred minimized the plan as one option among “literally scores” of venues considered by the league. MLB officials had contacted the Trump administration about staging a game at a national park “similar to the Field of Dreams game,” according to the White House. An official from the National Park Service had already made a trip to Grand Teton to scout potential sites before pressure from local officials forced Manfred to abandon the idea.

“We obviously would not bring a game to a community that has concerns about the venue, and we will not continue to evaluate Grand Teton National Park as a potential site,” he wrote in the Thursday letter, first reported by The Washington Post.

An MLB official declined to comment Thursday night.

“This is not a Presidential directive, nor is it being directed by the White House,” a White House spokesperson told The Washington Sun on Sunday. “It’s also not being driven by the Department of Interior.”

The league has hosted several games at nontraditional venues — including one at the historic Negro League ballpark in Birmingham, Alabama, and another at Fort Bragg in North Carolina — Manfred wrote, adding, “We have been careful to leave the selected sites better than when we arrived.”

He characterized the inquiry into Grand Teton as “initial due diligence.”

Teton County Commissioner Luther Propst said that he first spotted Frank Lands, a deputy director for the National Park Service, at Grand Teton last week.

The Teton County Commission and the Jackson Town Council unanimously approved draft letters on Monday objecting to the baseball game idea, Propst said.

“It crystallizes these issues in a way that everybody can understand — that the Trump administration is undertaking a very hostile approach to managing public lands,” Propst said Thursday night.

“It’s a war on our public lands,” he added. “This one we won, but every month there are another dozen assaults.”

In August, The Sun reported that officials within the Trump administration had lobbied the National Park Service regarding a potential land exchange benefitting a private developer who sought to construct an access road between an external property and Yosemite National Park.
entries.author: Gavin J. Quinton
